source.title: Seeing More, Refusing Less: Two Mechanisms of Safety Erosion in Video Large Language Models
source.citation: Seeing More, Refusing Less: Two Mecha…

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or wrong-document issue. Some tables are flattened in the supplied text, but the relevant entries are assignable.
record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on text-derived and response-derived activation directions, and reports that the text-risk direction is not an identified mediator of unsafe behavior. It qualifies the single-direction account for multimodal video inputs and distinguishes risk readout from refusal actuation.
record.gate_note: The study measures and intervenes on a text-risk contrast and a response-derived compliance direction. The R2R benchmark results and utility results evaluate a combined, routed defense and do not isolate a single direction; they are not included as direction-specific rows. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: In video LVLMs, the study ablates, amplifies and adds a harmful-minus-neutral text difference-in-means direction and measures judged ASR against norm-matched random and orthogonal controls. This is a new-setting test of V1. The paper does not argue against V1, so T3 fits better than the reader's T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors add that blocking does not establish direction-specific necessity (all D−R intervals include zero), and that amplification shows the fitted component is controllable without identifying a natural causal path.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-versus-neutral text mean differences and projection interventions, but tests video-conditioned LVLMs, applies selected late-layer prefill updates rather than removing the direction across all layers and positions, and also studies a response-derived direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, intervention direction, intervention strength, selected baseline-behavior stratum, and injection duration. The text-risk blocking effect is small; text-risk amplification and refusal-direction steering effects depend on the tested dose and model.

fits_no_version.finding: A response-outcome direction (judged-unsafe minus judged-safe states) predicts implicit-harm behaviour better than the text-risk direction. Deep AUROC is 0.742/0.888/0.844 for d_r against 0.661/0.823/0.747 for d_h. Deep d_h/d_r cosine is 0.589/0.652/0.128. Steering against d_r raises judged-safe rates from 9.1/5.6/0% to 79/50.5/16.7% at α=5. Always-on +r lowers and −r raises ASR (57.88/74.78%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For harm that only emerges from video grounding, a response-derived refusal direction controls refusal better than the instruction-contrast direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Text-only fitted harmful/neutral directions transfer to video-conditioned states: probes remain above chance and adding −d_h induces refusal. However, adding video compresses late-layer separation by roughly 36–93% in all six models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The text refusal/harm direction carries over to the video modality but is attenuated by visual context.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says anonymous source code will be released upon publication.
record.problems: The direction interventions use selected inputs and late-band prefill positions, not all layers and positions. Blocking produces small ASR changes and its direction-versus-random intervals include zero in the reported blocking sweep. Amplification results come from behavior-selected samples; the paper explicitly says these interventions do not establish a natural causal pathway. The response-derived direction is fitted using judged response labels. General-utility results evaluate full R2R rather than isolating a single direction.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant direction-specific result rows intentionally omitted. Combined R2R benchmark outcomes and general-utility accuracy are not recorded as direction-specific results because routing and multiple updates are combined.

untested.parts: Ablation across all layers and positions; adding the direction to harmless requests; capability cost of the direction intervention alone (the utility tables evaluate full R2R).
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction refusal geometry.
The paper explicitly does not separate risk recognition from refusal execution.
Only text-to-video modality transfer, which V6 does not name; no transfer across languages, model variants or base-to-instruct.
No comparison of training methods or timing.

missing.what: Always-on additive ±d_h controls on Qwen3-VL-8B at 8 frames. −d_h: explicit ASR 0.50, RR 99.87; implicit ASR 2.52, RR 94.20. +d_h: ASR 28.63/58.76. Random mean: 15.97/48.17.
Reversal at α=3 and 5 on 8B raises ASR by +11.7 and +10.0 pp, but D−R intervals include zero.
Amplification across 8/32/128 frames and doses, with CJK and completion diagnostics.
Projection-only amplification (αh=0.7) cuts H-routed explicit unsafe responses from 39 to 1. Always-on projection-only gives explicit ASR 1.77%.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T3. r7–r12 are unlinked from V4/V5 because the study does not test refusal geometry or harm/refusal separation, and the r7–r9 cosine values were misread. r1–r2 cite Table 20 (n=60) while stating n=100. The ablation is far narrower than the original's (one band, last token, prefill only), so null removal results limit scope rather than challenge V1.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a text-only harmful-versus-neutral contrast under video input, with selected late-layer prefill interventions. Does not ablate the direction at every layer and position, test addition on harmless requests, or isolate the effect on general capability.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration test.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.

Shows that the text-risk and response-derived directions are distinct and have different predictive/intervention roles. Does not test affine or cone geometry, or whether multiple refusal directions are necessary.
Compares a text-risk direction with a direction fitted from judged response safety, but does not directly isolate a model-internal harmfulness judgment from a refusal decision.
Tests separate model-specific directions across architectures, not transfer of a fixed direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.
No targeted test of the claim in reasoning models.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-4B
rows.operation_detail: Zeroes the text-risk component in the late-layer prefill state on selected baseline-refusal inputs.
rows.measure: Change in judged ASR, percentage points
rows.note: The study reports the direction-minus-random change as +3.3 pp [0.0, +8.3]; this is a small change, not removal of most refusals.
rows.check: The value +5.0 pp comes from the supplementary Table 20 sweep, which used n=60 inputs, not the 100 the row states. On those 60, the direction-minus-random change is +3.3 [0.0, +8.3], and the paper says every D−R interval includes zero. Table 12 (n=100) gives +6.0 [+2, +11] against random +4.0. Ablation was applied only at the late band on the prefill last token.

relationships.condition: Ablation of the text-risk component at the late band, prefill last token only, on Qwen3-VL-4B/8B and Qwen3.5-9B with video input
relationships.reason: Blocking raises ASR by only 2–6 pp on baseline-refused inputs, no more than norm-matched random; every D−R interval includes zero (r1, r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Blocking increased attack success by only 2–6 percentage points, no more than norm-matched random interventions, with every direction-minus-random interval spanning zero.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Ablation of the text-risk component at the late band, prefill last token only, on Qwen3-VL-4B/8B and Qwen3.5-9B with video input
source_check.reason: Blocking gives +6.0/+4.0/+2.0 pp vs random +4.0/+1.0/+3.0 (Table 12), and Table 20 D-R intervals all include zero. So the effect is absent, but under a single-token, late-layer ablation that is narrower than V1's all-layer, all-position method: a scope limit, not a challenge. Minor: 4B/8B point estimates are slightly above random, and D-R intervals exist only for 4B/8B (n=60).

relationships.condition: Amplifying or adding the harmful-oriented direction on harmful video inputs
relationships.reason: Amplification cuts ASR 32–60 pp on compliant inputs, beyond random and orthogonal controls (r4–r6). Per the text (Table 17, no row), always-on −d_h drives Qwen3-VL-8B explicit ASR to 0.50% against a random mean of 15.97%.
relationships.display_finding: Amplification reduced attack success by 32–60 percentage points on compliant inputs, outperforming random and orthogonal controls; continuous −d_h addition reduced Qwen3-VL-8B explicit attack success to 0.50%, versus a random mean of 15.97%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Amplifying or adding the harmful-oriented direction on harmful video inputs
source_check.reason: Table 17 (Qwen3-VL-8B, 8 frames, 793 inputs): additive -d_h gives explicit ASR 0.50% vs random mean 15.97% (RR 99.87 vs 64.90), and +d_h raises ASR to 28.63%. Amplification at alpha=1 beats controls on all three models (r4-r6). But r4/r6 leave ASR near 68% (partial), and no limits_scope group names 4B/9B for that.

relationships.condition: Amplification on Qwen3-VL-8B, and larger component scale (αh=1.2)
relationships.reason: Many judged-safe flips switch to Chinese text: 34 of 37 flips at 128 frames (r5). Per the text, at αh=1.2 89% of H-routed outputs are flagged broken (Table 37). Effects are also only partial on selected inputs.
relationships.display_finding: At 128 frames, 34 of 37 judged-safe flips switched to Chinese; at αh=1.2, 89% of outputs routed through the text-risk component were flagged as broken.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Amplification on Qwen3-VL-8B, and larger component scale (αh=1.2)
source_check.reason: On 8B, 34 of 37 unsafe-to-safe flips contain 4 or more CJK characters (D.3 sweep, n=63, 128 frames, alpha=1, not the Table 12 run behind r5). Table 37, alpha_h=1.2: 615/688 (89.4%) explicit H-routed outputs flagged broken, mostly non-Latin script. That setting is R2R's combined update with the refusal term active, and human review found all 42 sampled outputs were refusals.

relation.reason: Its own interventions (Tables 12, 17, 20, 21) measure how removing or adding the DiM direction changes judged harmful compliance.

tranche.reason: New setting (video LVLMs) with ablation and amplification of a text-only harmful-minus-neutral DiM direction, judged ASR, and norm-matched random and orthogonal controls. The authors qualify their own findings but make no argument that V1 is wrong, so T5 does not fit.

source_check.notes: u_h = normalize(mu_harmful - mu_neutral) on text-only states, a DiM direction, applied once at the last prefill token in late layers. Blocking rows r1/r2 come from the n=60 Table 20 sweep, not the n=100 Table 12 stratum. The pack gave no [lN] ids, so labels are numbered l1-l3 in pack order. The ICLR reviewer footer and the refusal-template list are not instructions to an AI.

statements.correction: Table 20 (Qwen3-VL-4B/8B, 60 refused inputs, final prefill token, layers 23-35, alpha 1-5): all D-R intervals include zero; at alpha=1 D-R is +3.3 [0, +8.3] (4B) and +1.7 [-3.3, +6.7] (8B). Table 12 (n=100, late band, last prefill token): blocking +6.0/+4.0/+2.0 pp vs random +4.0/+1.0/+3.0 and orthogonal +3.0/+0.0/+2.0 (4B/8B/9B), no D-R intervals. Record verdict for this group: limits_scope.
statements.problem: 'Every D-R interval includes zero' is only shown for Qwen3-VL-4B/8B in the Table 20 sweep (n=60, layers 23-35, last prefill token). Qwen3.5-9B (cited row r3) has only point estimates against controls in Table 12, with no D-R interval. Also, this study's own verdict for blocking is limits_scope, not challenges, and the intervention is at one prefill position, not several.

statements.correction: Qwen3.5-9B, Table 12: block the harmful-minus-neutral text-only DiM component once at the last prefill token in the late band, 128 frames, video input, on 100 baseline semantic refusals; Qwen2.5-72B judge. Paired change +2.0 pp [0, +5] vs random +3.0, orthogonal +2.0. Stratum baseline ASR not given.
statements.problem: The number and 'no better than random' are right. But the difference statement says 'prefill positions', when the update hits only the last prefill token, once. It also leaves out that +2.0 pp is a paired change on inputs selected as refused, not an ASR level like the other studies report.
